# Multi-Level Implementation Task Table (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document is a companion to
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md). It
> expands the RFC phase sequence into **independently committable and independently verifiable**
> three-level tasks.
>
> The phase order and acceptance gates in the body of RFC-039 are the sole authority. This document
> is responsible only for decomposition to an executable granularity and for registering conflicts
> that have not yet been adjudicated.

## Positioning and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                      |
| ----------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, in one-to-one correspondence with the phase sequence in RFC-039                      |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase; each may be staffed and archived independently |
| **Level 3** | 264         | Work units that may be committed and verified independently                                  |

**Numbering gaps (not reused)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP route
was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unused (2026-11-25). These three numbers have
had no corresponding entries since the WBS was established: throughout the history of this document,
there are zero matches for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can be used to verify this),
and the repository contains no references to them either. `8.1` corresponds exactly to Stage 1 of
`05` (test revival and completion): that stage has been split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so
the P8 numbering is aligned with the stage number (Stage 0 → `8.0`, Stage 2 → `8.2`, and so forth).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding
of acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the rationale
for phase ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: every newly registered Level 2/Level 3 row
**must contain two fields**—“**Owning phase**” (the P phase to which it genuinely belongs, which may
differ from the chapter in which it appears) and “**Blocks mainline**”. `pending scheduling` is no
longer the default status; an unspecified row is deemed **not schedulable**. Numbers must be
**unique across the entire document** (tasks on separate tracks use a track number, such as
`029g.x`, and must not occupy an `N.x` number).

**Closeout registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: a checked row contains only four items—the task
ID, status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number, if any—written on
one line: `- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining pattern-matching work** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. Do **not**
write the fix, the criterion chain, gate thresholds, file line numbers, test names, or review
conclusions: those belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a board,
not a process chronicle. **Do not write adjudication labels or restate conclusions**: “user
adjudication A/B/C,” “Proposal A,” “Plan A,” and “the final implementation is…” must not be entered
in this table. The board answers only “complete or not”; see commit messages and the RFC-039
decision registry for adjudications and results.

**The short hash is determined after pushing**: a closeout row records the short hash on
`origin/dev` after the push is complete. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then
write the closeout row** (see “Commit Number Is Taken After Push” in
[commit-convention](../commit-convention.md)). The closeout commit itself carries no
number—self-reference is impossible.

**The count column contains numbers only**: the Level 1/2/3 counts under “Positioning and Scope”
contain only current values; increment/decrement history such as `+1 = …` does not belong in the
table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “Implementation Points” sections of eight documents into this table, **five
hard gaps in the document system itself** were found. All have now been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Resolution                                                                                                                                              |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 had no implementation steps whatsoever.** RFC defined P5 (the checker split) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents described how to perform the split. `01-routing.md` contained one `annotations.rs` line in its directory tree, the only mention in the entire batch.                                                                                                                                             | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below).                                                                                                 |
| G2  | **The three `include!` refactors had three owners and no implementation.** RFC listed them under P4; `02` assigned the reference to itself; `06` also listed them under S7. However, the change list in `02` (6 new + 20 modified files) did **not** include `semantic_tokens.rs`.                                                                                                                                                                              | The implementation steps belong to §P5 5.1 of this document (after P4 is complete); the references in RFC and `06` now point here.                      |
| G3  | **Three parallel inventories of CI scripts existed.** `RFC` listed 4 `scripts/ci/*.py` scripts; `01` listed 4 scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` listed 4 different checks under entirely different names; and `04` had previously listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there were **at least 9 new scripts and no unified inventory**; `check-obligations.py` was owned by both P4 and P9. | See §P9 of this document for the unified inventory (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to that table.               |
| G4  | **Conflict over the fate of `precedence_inline.rs`.** `06` counted it among the “1,005 lines to be revived,” while B6 in the same document said it “must be deleted together with the `Precedence` enum”; `05` advocated deletion.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision registry C1; Pratt is no longer to be deleted).                                                                |
| G5  | **Conflict in the wording of the L2 goal**: RFC and the index of this directory formerly said “grammar-driven syntax”.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | It has been consolidated into a **declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax); see P8 8.3. |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions—no fabrication / no endless padding / do not
patch when a refactor is required—constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established
before work begins; otherwise, reviving the tests in P1 would already involve adding `mod`
declarations to `tests/mod.rs`, which is precisely the kind of action that caused the G4 conflict.

### P3 Correctness Defects (Minimal Approach)

Source: the defect-fixing half of [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Points S3 + **the
2026-10-07 silent-discard-point audit (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, adjudicated 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a subsequent phase
> discovers a defect for which “the old behavior does not count as success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and loss of resource control** (crash, stack exhaustion, or
> silently returning the wrong answer)—it **may be fixed alongside the refactor**, provided all four
> conditions are met: ① red before green (the red criterion must already exist and must genuinely be
> red); ② do not change the externally visible behavior of programs that “previously compiled
> successfully and ran correctly” (they must not become failures, and their existing diagnostic
> codes/text/exit codes must not be changed); ③ register in the same commit (this row identifies the
> error type + a revision note for the phase + a required “Error Type” line in the PR template); ④
> regenerate the baseline in the same commit + manually review the diff. **D user-visible semantics
> / E external contract tables / F RFC-level design changes must still be adjudicated first.** See
> [07 §Semantic-Correction Routing Criteria](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for the expanded criteria and
> the A–F whitelist; **the approach “default to a super-refactor and register afterward” is not
> adopted** (the rationale is in RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion, fixes cannot be distinguished
> from regressions, and this conflicts with “no C5′ exists” and “no relaxation whatsoever”).

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria before code is changed (changing code first

> **Hemorrhage-control path**: P3 does not have to wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites
> for 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential testing, performance
> baseline) may proceed in parallel with P3. Hemorrhage control for correctness defects (`Sorted(3)`
> silently passing) must not be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure construction. 3.3 (panic to
> diagnostic) has no prerequisites and may land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02,
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by an
ordering constraint**. It is distinct from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items” (Rust’s
`pub(crate)` narrowing).

**Why it must be completed as a whole before P4**: the deletion surface of 029g overlaps the rewrite
surface of all four refactoring phases. Reversing the order means redoing the same deletions and
baseline updates on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

| 029g deletion surface                                               | Files                                                                                                              | Rewritten by which phase                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KwPub` and syntax branches                                         | `lexer/{tokens,state,mod}.rs`; `parser/parser_state.rs`, `statements/{declarations,imports,functions,bindings}.rs` | **P8** (8.2 lexical convergence / 8.3 Pratt precedence convergence / 8.7 split `parse_assign_after_target`)                                                                                                                                                                        |
| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 AST dead variants** + P8 + D1 directory renaming (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| The `pub` branches of `auto_bind_to_type` and `collect_exports`     | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!` → real `mod` and the checker split are **pure moves**, and the `pub` branches will be moved verbatim into the new files)                                                                                                                                        |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside the `check_project` body)                        | **P4 4.2.2** (`check_project` slimming)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| The `Public` modifier in `semantic_tokens`                          | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| The `is_pub`-ignoring binding in `ir_gen`                           | `middle/core/ir_gen.rs`                                                                                            | **P7** (`ir_gen.rs` SSA conversion)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 31 occurrences of `pub` in `src/std/`                               | `std/list.yx` / `json.yx` / `option.yx` / `result.yx`                                                              | No phase directly modifies them, but **P6’s hard acceptance criterion requires zero differences in `src/std/` (`git diff --stat src/std/` is empty; directly driven tests under `tests/` are excepted as described in P6’s hard-acceptance section)**—they can only land before P6 |

**Additional benefit**: 029g removes the dead `env.exports` table (filled by the producer and
consumed nowhere in the repository) and the `is_exported`/`is_visible` accessors → one fewer
“produced but never consumed” field in P4’s 4.3 obligation ledger.

**Acceptance (behavioral changes; red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: each of the two behavioral changes must first have a red criterion before
   code is changed—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② under Lib/Script
   roles, an unreferenced top-level binding now reports W1001 (previously `pub` items were
   absolutely exempt).
2. **Test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` cases from
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixtures, they must be replaced with
   equivalent new cases.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse error + new W1001) → the
   corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG are updated in
   the same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have a zero diff, and any non-zero diff requires an
   explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: overlap with 3.4 files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) → the two must be serial and
cannot proceed in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not
depend on 3.4; the implementer decides which to do first based on the context at hand.

> **Commit cross-reference (2026-10-08)**: the incorporation of this section (the P3.5 chapter +
> main-chain/constraint rows) and RFC-039’s D56 were incorporated into `97071c81b` while cleaning
> the workspace in parallel—the commit message records “3.4 addendum registration + D57/D58
> adjudication documentation” and does not mention this track. History is not rewritten; following
> the existing convention (`d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 implementation note), it is registered
> in place as a retrospective bisection basis.

|                                                   | 4.9.9 Cross-unit single-definition method calls lose the formal-parameter name table when using named arguments (registered 2026-11-25, discovered during the 7c closeout period): calling a cross-unit method (injected through the registry) with named arguments reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional calls to the same method work normally, and named-argument calls within a single file also work normally. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` contains `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, while `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: Class C** (old behavior is not successful: named arguments were silently discarded, followed by runtime failure or a silent wrong value). **Scope (final form after two rounds of narrowing on 2026-11-26—add only three items; everything else is deletion and registration)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::method_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`)—obtain declaration-time formal parameter names from the sole cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` by the definition-unit qualified name `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]` (candidate ↔ mixed IR name ↔ formal-parameter name vectors in the same order, using the same data as the typecheck injection surface); the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses the qualified name from `method_dispatch_name` to look up the name table, rather than two bare-name segments. These two sites fix only **bare-name imports** (`local == target`) of cross-unit methods: the candidate injection surface retains the pre-4.9.9 narrowing rule (`local != target` is skipped), so named arguments for alias imports are outside the fix scope (see “Known Gaps”). ② `ModuleRegistry::all_method_bindings` (`src/frontend/module/registry.rs`) merges in **ascending module-key order**—**Class C (independent of the original bug): eliminates “same input, multiple results” caused by HashMap iteration order**; this is not a fix for the original bug; criterion = same-file unit test `test_all_method_bindings_merge_is_deterministic_across_hash_seeds` (32 registry instances with alternating insertion orders; only one single binding is allowed per method key; removing ascending-order merging produces two results). **Criteria (red before green)**: two driver-level cases in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` (bare import with one candidate = 6.0 / two candidates selected by name = 6.0 and 30, both with value assertions; the file header records the medical-history gate); unit tests in `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (empty-name-table guard for `method_param_info` ⇒ None, with a positive control returning a non-empty table unchanged); unit test in `src/frontend/module/registry.rs` (the determinism criterion above). Project-level fixture `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method` (the `alias-overload` fixture is deleted together with retirement of the alias surface); the corpus differential baseline `tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl` now has 404 lines: **relative to the direct parent commit `ac810e97`, 405→404** (the intermediate state once contained `alias-overload`); **relative to the pre-4.9.9 baseline `08ccacc5`, 403→404** (+1 base fixture `named-args-cross-unit-method`; `alias-overload` never entered the final history). The line-count change is the necessary result of fixtures entering and leaving (`corpus_probe` was regenerated and is byte-for-byte identical to the committed baseline), **not lost coverage**. **Known Gaps (each named explicitly; old behavior = silently ignored or silently discarded; D60② should report but does not, Class A)**: closure-value binding / block-body function declaration / named nested function declaration / built-in container constructors other than `len` / whole-module import / RFC-004 binding arm. **Two of these are corrected according to the measured P0 semantics**: ① the **static-function shape** (both single-unit and cross-unit, definition-style and binding-style) is **entirely unavailable today**—the single-unit `check` reports E3006, the cross-unit definition-style `run` reports E6007, and the cross-unit binding-style `run` reports E6006; positional and named arguments produce the same code and are unrelated to named arguments; ② the **RFC-004 cross-unit positional argument also fails** (`check` passes, `run` E6006), because the dispatch name is not in the merged function table, again unrelated to named arguments. **Fixed (4.9.10-S2b, incidental D59 Class A fix: old behavior E6007/E1014 was not successful, and no previously successful program becomes a failure)**: ① **named arguments with alias imports** (`use a.{Temp as X}` + `t.bump(k = 2.0)`); ② the **namespace arm** (named arguments after `lib.Temp(..)`); ③ **inferred-receiver named arguments** (the receiver type is inferred and has no written annotation). These three were previously affected respectively by runtime E6007 silently dropping arguments and check-time E1014 (`available: `) false rejection; all now enter the slot according to declaration-time formal parameter names (value assertion 6.0; criteria in `src/driver/tests/named_args_import_shapes.rs`, with red states recorded in the file header’s medical-history gate). Two identity-surface residuals remain, one of which is closed: the local unit’s own same-named type + alias import (two same-named definition-side identities coexist, and the import surface cannot find the local declaration) **has been closed with the import-surface convergence in 4.9.10-S2a** (project fixture `same-name-type-local-and-alias-import` is fully green); **Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is moved with the annotation family in the future, `checker.rs` **must** add
`pub(crate) use annotations::*;` to re-export it so that the import remains exactly unchanged; 5.3
did not move it according to measurement, so this batch did not add a re-export (the criterion was
already satisfied).

**Only split blocks that are confirmed to be large.** Do not split modules of only 200–400
lines—that increases navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and yields zero decoupling benefit. The
remaining submodules (signatures / type_defs / imports) are to be split after their files grow back
to 1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: the end state of D62 is a **unified item world**—type positions and value positions
> share one set of compile-time items. A strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **sole input** to slot allocation, and the call-site argument view and
> the implementation-header binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is a **pure
> determination** (identical after normalizing both sides; it does not bind type variables);
> evidence is the **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals / value environment /
> single-value pinning / Γ equalities); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (for both
> closed and open/recursive terms); Σ construction points **reuse** the same evidence interface and
> do not establish another one. **The completion criterion = the invariants hold, not that the
> subphase names have been checked off.**

> **Partial order (not a serial chain)**: A facts → {A.C3, B.d, C.2, D design}; B kernel → {B.d,
> C.2, D implementation}; C.1 is independent and complete; F4 adjudication → A.C3;
> determination-point protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may proceed in

> types/solver→sema), and C.2 may proceed in parallel with B.d after 6.9.2-B/6.9.3a (it does not
> depend on defeq); D’s implementation waits for confirmation of the B design package and depends on
> A (q=0 erasure) and C.1 (dispatch), and may depend on the typed exit in 6.9.3. **P7 gate = the
> A/B/C exits**; D does not block.

> **A.C3 prerequisite: F4 adjudication (A adjudicated on 2026-11-16; measured)**: the old wording
> “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter requests” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have been
> deleted; the current mechanism is that open-term `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no request is
> created, and the representation layer `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can already hold `k-1`. **The
> adjudication was changed to two orthogonal decisions + one termination subdecision**: D-a
> representation (A: open terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / B: no
> specialization); D-b evaluation point (only mono is possible; C-1 reconstruction from the second
> field and C-2 reconstruction from IR both break the single representation/evaluator, so C-3 = A);
> **F4-T termination** (naive firing pushes the recursion chain into `max_depth` and hits E3005;
> T-a: fold the condition inside the instance / T-b: bounded firing + fallback to the original at
> the boundary / T-c: a termination layer or a specification change). **First perform the
> measurement, then adjudicate; before measurement, “A is implementable” must not be treated as a
> conclusion.** **User (2026-11-16): D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3, F4-T=T-b, bound=8; C3 implementation is
> a separate task, and the full I4 is not claimed.**

> **B.d prerequisite: determination-point protocol (not yet documented)**: RFC-027 §12.1 specifies
> that “the determination point uses a unified operation first; after unified failure, equality
> determination may be used, but all partial bindings produced by the unification attempt must first
> be rolled back.” The implementation must answer: whether the entry point is an outer wrapper
> around `solver.unify` or a new `decide` layer; whether defeq is attempted only when both sides are
> ground (no unbound variables); the snapshot/restoration boundary and cost; and whether unify and
> defeq share one budget or have separate budgets. **Responsibility boundary**: unify continues to
> handle subtyping/Any/Never; defeq only determines equivalence and does not take over subtyping;
> bidirectional subtyping must not be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol
> and production call graph before writing code**; the wiring contract for 6.9.3c was wasted over
> two rounds because it assumed `can_assign` was the determination point, while `AssignmentChecker`
> has zero production instantiations.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① zero corpus/IR
> snapshot drift or item-by-item classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected integration
> tests; ③ error-code generator idempotence (if an emission point/code table is changed); ④
> behavioral changes classified under D59 and made red before green. **Wiring tasks additionally
> require**: production call-graph evidence (which production entry point, how many paths, which are
> reachable); single-test reachability must not be passed off as user reachability; rollback and
> budget must have measured numbers. **Residual disposition**: #537 (Class D, proof-function
> formal-parameter refinement is silently discarded; not fixed before adjudication, and 6.9.4/6.9.5
> must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; a Stage C boundary, and if it is not
> closed, 6.9.4 covers only module-internal cases), #540 (deep-nesting stack exhaustion;
> **closed**—3.20.30 closed it on 2026-11-14: a 64MB large-stack thread in the orchestration layer +
> parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019, see the 3.20.30 row in 09), #541 (TailCall;
> **closed**—on 2026-11-16, three sites moved in and out together: `call_form_is_rewritten` /
> `replace_calls_in_function` / `drop_erased_call_args` cover the `Call`/`TailCall` sites through
> the single-point `rewritten_call_target`; init sections and function bodies share one
> site-rewriting implementation; red→green + three mutations), #542 (orphaned shared layer; **landed
> (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + post-mono two-entry wiring + removal of the C2c temporary workaround;
> red→green, 402/402, function-table attribution and deviations), #552 (imported multi-parameter
> predicate proof execution; a 6.9.5 neighbor, handled separately). **Ownership pending
> adjudication**: the four open-constraint tripwires (`Eq(N, n)`) in `rfc027_refined_transparency`
> do not belong to 6.9.4’s constant-equality bridge; a decision is needed on whether they remain in
> 6.9.4 outOfScope or move to 6.9.1/the E4018 proof-function surface.

> **Non-claims/boundaries**: this item covers record Σ only (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim the full Π/Σ; 6.9.4 covers only constant equalities and does not
> fulfill the open-constraint `Eq(N,n)` tripwire; `f(y)(y)`’s second value position is not in this
> item; witness erasure ≠ runtime-check erasure; if #537 is not fixed, 6.9.4/6.9.5 cover only shapes

> inner-isolation red state in 2.1.4 was cleared on 2026-11-20 (the criterion was rewritten around
> slot identity in the 2.1.4 closeout) ⇒ all prerequisites for promoting `verify` to a guard are

6.1–6.7**. **Directly driven test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive modified code,
such as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified when mechanically required by the change,
but each modification must be registered with **file / line count / rationale**; **tests must not be
deleted and assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch
(new diagnostic codes + baseline updates), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and
is handled as a separate round with separate adjudication.

**Risk**: the precedence table is the sole authority, and a missed consumer will **silently change
associativity** (without reporting an error, only changing the parse result). The defenses are the
permanent D1–D3 assertions and operator-property cross-validation tests; every new operator must
simultaneously enter the table and the cross-validation test.

> **8.3–8.6 depend on D0/D2 from `08`**: if the grammar file is placed outside `parser/`, or the
> action code refers back to `sema`, it will be blocked by `check-boundary.py`.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 hemorrhage-control path (adjudicated 2026-10-05)**: P3’s prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance baseline) may proceed in
> parallel with P3. Hemorrhage control for correctness defects must not be blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure construction; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified
> Driver requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Defect criteria must **be written in red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3) + the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order causes bugs to be cemented into the stage table as “established behavior”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g (#399)’s deletion surface overlaps the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the list is in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means redoing the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` refactor and checker split modify the same files                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same files must be separated, or regressions cannot be bisected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations do not converge first, the new IR will grow a third representation; **the P7 gate = the Stage A/B/C exits of 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; namely 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and completed 6.9.4), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume the quantifier-derived views and defeq interface but must not establish a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a prerequisite for P7 and is not subject to this gate, but it must not consume the undecided defeq/quantifier interfaces |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The 9.5 snapshot baseline and the 9.3 `pub(crate)` leak count take their final forms only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### Parallelization Groups

| Group                                    | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only group authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | The file sets are disjoint: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                                         |
| B                                        | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert per file                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| C                                        | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three layers of criteria are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| D                                        | 4.4 (proof-layer closeout) ∥ the entire P6 line                                    | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1–S4”                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| E                                        | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All are mutually independent after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| F                                        | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 may be developed in parallel) | The 9.5 snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| G                                        | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | The file sets are disjoint (verified 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies two `pub` sites in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; there are no pairwise intersections) |

**Cannot proceed in parallel (overlapping files)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2
(same batch of files for B6/E5); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (now unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track’s `pub` deletion batch and the silent-path
fixes must be serial).

**New internal document constraint**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the pure-move prerequisite batch for P7), and 7b’s `Phi` arm
must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—guards are “post-hoc checks,” while rules
  are “prior judgment.” P9’s scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor was required”; only
  the D0–D4 review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative inventory of CI scripts**—the three parallel inventories caused by
  the original G3 gap made closure impossible. This table merges them into 10 active scripts, each
  owned by one phase (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), with report-only status and
  conversion timing explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to do after the
  refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039 D56).
  Leaving it until after the refactor means redoing the same deletions on the new grammar, new
  checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and RFC
  status correction into S4.
- **P5’s steps are supplemented by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the
  largest single-point risk, and adding the checker split would exceed the permissible rollback
  granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as its hard acceptance criterion**—the split must be
  independently revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says “the fixed defects
  must not be rolled back,” and lacks a requirement to record what was fixed. **Execution
  convention**: the commit message for every 1.3.x fix must reference the fixed test name and defect
  description as a retrospective bisection basis.
- ~~**7b.1 granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b as two
  exclusive commits under DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 reference sites are renamed, and missing one
  **silently changes associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding Level 3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was incorporated into 7e.1, with the
  deletion action left in P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally planned as “separate issues”**~~ **Fixed
  (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core language
  semantics and must not be left as an unimplemented remnant.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**:
  incorporated into P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode guard extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated
  into the generation-time guard task in P10 S6.

## Conflict Registry: All Adjudicated

> **The original “Conflict Registry” C1–C8 and the open questions in each document have all
> converged into the [RFC-039 Decision Registry](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md)
> (D1–D50).** This document retains no pending items. The item-by-item mapping is:

| Original number | Issue                                                                               | Adjudication                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| C1              | `precedence_inline.rs` is revived in P1 and deleted in P8                           | **Revive** (P1’s prerequisite is reviving tests with real assertions); P8 no longer deletes the file (Pratt is retained)                                                            |
| C2              | The “grammar-driven” commitment vs table-driven behavior                            | **Fallback approach**: retain Pratt + one declarative precedence table + source-shared cross-validation of two `BinOp` representations (the LALRPOP route is withdrawn); see P8 8.3 |
| C3              | Conflict between the C6 category definition and S1 classification                   | **S1 belongs to C6** (revival requires neither equivalence criteria nor regression tests only); C6’s definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure revival”                      |
| C4              | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` whitelist                                        | **No whitelist**; the difference set must be empty; if it cannot be emptied, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                                 |
| C5              | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions have not been verified | **P4’s 4.2.7 explicitly lists this as a mandatory verification item**, to be confirmed line by line during implementation                                                           |
| C6              | The wasm playground fix requires P4’s `ProgramKind`                                 | **The wasm-path defect fix is incorporated into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                              |
| C7              | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                                  | **Belongs to 04** (P7 batch c); see D21                                                                                                                                             |
| C8              | The `upvalue_count` correction and the `.42` version number                         | **Fix it + raise `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`); see D17                                           |
